questions: Does the s-bend finish rate recover above 0.10 at 0.095 m, or does it stay at 0 as at 0.09 m? If it stays at 0, the s-bend overshoot is set by yaw gain and the track should return to 0.10 m.
Does the oval finish rate hold at or above 0.5? If it falls back to 0.45 or below, the oval gain is not coming from wheel_track alone.
Does s-bend max_error move below 0.063 m? If it still clusters at about 0.0645 m, the overshoot is not from turn authority and the next lever is sensor forward offset (y) or base_speed.
Is steering_oscillation on the s-bend still near 0.27 to 0.43? If it rises well above 0.43 with no line-loss gain, reduce kp or raise kd on the Integrator side.

intent: Keep the five-sensor ±0.04 m row, mass 0.6 kg, body and wheel radius from iteration 2, and set wheel_track to 0.095 m, between the iteration 2 (0.10 m, score 321) and iteration 3 (0.09 m, score 303) designs. The aim is to keep most of the oval gain while restoring s-bend completions by limiting yaw overshoot on bends. Expected result: oval finish rate about 0.5 to 0.55, s-bend finish rate 0.05 to 0.10, s-bend max_error below 0.063 m, and a total score near or above 321. Gains and base_speed remain the Integrator's choice.
learning: Iterations 2 and 3 show that narrowing wheel_track raises oval finishes but cuts s-bend completions, so the best setting is between 0.09 and 0.10 m. If 0.095 m gives a score above 321, narrow further only with a bend-specific fix. If it gives a score below 321, return to 0.10 m and test sensor forward offset (y = 0.06 m) as the next geometry lever.
rationale: Iteration 3 narrowed wheel_track from 0.10 to 0.09 m and scored 303, below iteration 2's 321. The oval improved: finish rate rose from 0.45 to 0.65, progress from 0.86 to 0.92, and completion time from 1.73 to 1.79 s. The s-bend got worse: finish rate fell from 0.10 to 0.00, progress from 0.67 to 0.33, and max_error rose from 0.0627 to 0.0645 m. Steering oscillation on the s-bend dropped from 0.43 to 0.27, so the s-bend failure is not jitter. It looks like the extra yaw gain overshoots on the bends. Sensing is not the limit, since the five-sensor row at ±0.04 m is still the best layout tested. Mass has been 0.6 kg since iteration 2 and was not varied. Because the s-bend completions are worth far more than the oval gain, and the 0.10 m design is the only one with s-bend completions, I will interpolate to wheel_track 0.095 m. This keeps the oval gain from narrowing while reducing the bend overshoot. I expect the oval finish rate to land around 0.5 to 0.55 and the s-bend finish rate to recover to roughly 0.05 to 0.10, for a score near the iteration 2 level. Only wheel_track changes, so the next race isolates how the score responds between 0.09 and 0.10 m.
